name: Forest Preserve Experience
org: Friends of the Forest Preserves, Forest Preserves of Cook County and the Housing Authority of Cook County
what_you_do: A paid summer job on a crew of 12 teens. You remove invasive plants, pick up litter and clean rivers and lakes in your local forest preserve. You also learn job skills and go on field trips and canoe outings.
who_can_apply: Housing Authority of Cook County residents or voucher holders who live in the south suburbs. Ages 14 to 19 by the start of the program, in high school or a recent graduate.
pay_detail: The Forest Preserves page says $15.50 an hour. The Friends 2025 FAQ says $15 an hour.
duration: 5 weeks starting in late June or early July, about 24 to 25 hours a week
deadline_text: Last cycle the Housing Authority sent application materials in early March and applications closed April 30. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: If you qualify, the Housing Authority of Cook County contacts you in early March with the application. It has interview questions about why you want to work outdoors. Questions: joy@fotfp.org.
notes: Only for families with the Housing Authority of Cook County. If you miss more than three days, you lose your spot. There are no breaks for trips or summer school. Rides leave from Pace bus stops. The two official pages list a bit different pay and hours, so ask when you are hired. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work paper from school.
